question: Kidney cancer's textbook triad is blood in the urine, pain in the side and a lump you can feel. How many patients have all three?
answer: Under 1 in 10. Each sign appears in only a minority of patients, and all three together mostly in advanced disease. Most kidney cancers are now found by chance, on scans done for something else, before any symptom at all. The textbook triad describes the late case that doctors of an earlier era saw most.
move: Every extra detail in a classic picture makes fewer real cases fit it.
ask: Which classic picture of a problem do I hold, and how few real cases match every detail?
trap: About half, since each of the three is the classic sign.
source: Holland-Frei Cancer Medicine, renal cancer chapter
reference: Kufe et al. (eds), Holland-Frei Cancer Medicine, 6th edition, BC Decker, 2003
